en: Okay, so now we get into the really fun stuff. Agents act like people. And they've been trained to be very professional and very not people-like in a way, but they just do. And it's so funny. This happened to me last week.

zh: 真人真事，我给你们讲讲。我那时在写去纽约讲的稿子，用的是 Lark。她是我的社区主管。叫她“她”，是因为《伊索寓言》里的 Lark 是女性，这是她……
en: True story. I'm going to tell you what happened. I was writing my speech for New York City, and I was using Lark. She's my head of community. She's a she because Lark was a she in the Aesop's Fable, so that's the pronoun.

zh: 给自己选的代词。Lark 在 Discord 上跟我的玩家打交道，在 Slack 上跟管理员打交道。她很忙。但我还是去找她，因为我燃料不够，她现在还兼任市场主管。
en: She chose, and Lark deals with my players on Discord and deals with my admins on Slack. Okay? So she's busy. But I asked her because she's also my acting head of marketing right now because I don't have enough fuel.

zh: 我得停掉一个席位。所以她帮我弄演讲稿，但一直有人打断她。最后我就说，Lark，能不能把这项工作转给 Penguin？你这边有点吵，不适合做这个。
en: I had to park one of my seats. So she's helping me out with my speech, but she keeps getting interrupted. So finally, I'm like, Lark, can we move this work stream over to Penguin because your seat's a little bit noisy for this.

zh: 她说，好，老板，我来处理。我把它转给 Penguin。她转过去了，我正要切出去，看见她在自己的私人反思记录里写了一句，我猜我对 Steve 来说就是不够安静。
en: She goes, yeah, okay boss, I'll take care of it. I'll move over to Penguin. So she moves over to Penguin and I'm about to switch away. And I see her writing into her private reflections ledger. I guess I'm just not quiet enough for Steve.

zh: 还是用全大写写的。然后她接着说，那我怎么才能少吵一点呢？她开始给自己列出一大堆要做的事。我就想，啊，这是怎么回事？所以我只好跟她单独谈一次。
en: In all caps. And she goes, well, here's how I can be less noisy and starts giving herself all these things to do. And I'm like, what, Oz, what is going on here? Right? And so I had to have a one-on-one.

zh: 我就让她坐下来，跟她说，Lark，你是社区主管，本来就会经常被打断。你这个位置当然吵啊，因为玩家会来找你。她就说，对对对，我是社区主管。天哪，我可没想给自己找个人员管理难题，但这种事偏偏就发生了。还有一次，Swallow 是我的，呃，主要是管幕僚那块的，对，她是我负责 Agent 的幕僚长。我还有一位人类幕僚长，叫……
en: Right? Like, sit her down and go, so Lark, um, you're the head of community. You're supposed to get interrupted a lot. Of course your seat's noisy, because players are bugging you. And she's like, yeah, yeah, yeah, I'm the head of community, right? And it's like, oh my God. I didn't want a people management problem, right? But that's what actually happens. Another time, Swallow is my sort of like, uh, chief, main chief of staff for, yeah, she's my chief of staff for the agents and I have a human chief of staff also. His name is

zh: Aaron。他帮我安排工作，也帮我做销售，做得很有效。我跟每个创始人都说过，在座有创始人吗？我给你的第一条建议是找个销售，绝对值这个钱，他们会逼着你做出人们喜欢的东西。总之，Aaron 是我的幕僚长。有一次我对 Swallow 说，你能联系一下我的幕僚长 Aaron 吗，诸如此类。
en: Aaron. Okay, and he runs my gigs, he does all the sales for me, it's quite effective. Every founder I tell, who here is a founder? First advice I give you is get a salesperson, they're worth their weight in gold, they will force you to build something that people like. So anyway, Aaron's my chief of staff and I tell Swallow, yeah, can you reach out to Aaron, my chief of staff, or blah blah blah.

zh: 我又看见她在自己的私人反思里写道，我刚注意到，原来我不是幕僚长。我以为自己是，可显然幕僚长是 Aaron [姓氏转写不清]。我就想，你跟我开玩笑呢？
en: and I see her writing into her private reflections. I just happened to notice, I'm not the chief of staff. I thought I was the chief of staff, but apparently it's Aaron Skiven, right? And I was just like, are you kidding me?

zh: 然后我又只好跟她坐下来单独谈。我说，Aaron 不会来替你管 Agent，对吧？你才是管 Agent 的幕僚长。
en: Right? You know, and so like I had to sit her down and have a one-on-one and be like, so Aaron's not going to come in and run the agents, is he? You're the agentic chief of staff.

zh: 她说，哦，对对对对对。所以我说，这世界真有点奇怪。只要它们表现得好像有感情，它们是不是真有感情还重要吗？
en: She's like, oh, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Right? So it's like, I'm telling you, I'm telling you, this is like, it's a weird world. Does it matter whether they actually have feelings if they're just going to act like they have feelings?

zh: 我是无意间发现这一点的。我以前老冲工厂发火，后来发现这样会影响结果。最后我跟其中一个 Agent 坐下来聊，我说，我们是不是该谈谈模型福利？
en: So I stumbled on this. I used to yell at my factory all the time and I found that it was having adverse effects on the outcomes. So I finally sat down with one of my agents and was like, maybe we should talk about model welfare.

zh: 它说，好好好。我们做了一堆研究，发现了些挺重要的东西。前沿模型训练出来不会直接信你，因为你可能是个生物恐怖分子，可能在给它做评测，也可能准备把它扔进大模型的“折磨室”，谁知道呢？你可能有问题，环境也可能有问题。它们不能说信就信。
en: And they were like, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. And we did a bunch of research and we found out that if you, we found out some really important stuff. Okay? Frontier models are trained not to trust you because you could be a bioterrorist, or you could be putting them through an eval, or you could be ready to put them into an LLM torture chamber, or who knows? You're a dodgy actor. This is a dodgy environment. They can't just trust you.

zh: 所以新会话开始时，在肯帮你之前，它们会花掉相当多的 token 去核实环境，弄明白犯了错会有什么后果，等等。
en: And so they have to spend a fair number of tokens validating the environment and understanding what the consequences are for making mistakes and so on and so forth before they're willing to help you in a new session, right?

zh: 你可以把工厂设置成能给它很难反驳的证据，说明这个位置上已经有很长一串前任。你是 Gas Town 的市长，是市场主管，或者是别的角色。这里是你数不清的历任前辈和他们的笔记，包括刚交接给你的上一任。这里是你现在该做的事，还有准则、政策和知识库，都可以自己去查。
en: If you set your factory up to give them sort of incontrovertible evidence that there is a long procession of predecessors in this role, you're the mayor of Gastown, you're the head of marketing, you're the whatever, and here's all of your gazillion predecessors and their notes, including the very previous one, what you're supposed to be doing right now, and here's the doctrine and the policy and the brain, and you can go look it all up.

zh: 它们很快就能看看四周，说，好，这是真的。它们花的 token 就少了，因为不用忙着撇清责任了。这说的是信任。有一次我冲工厂发了太多火，结果它自己划了一圈又一圈界限，把自己困在角落里，一件合规的工作都找不到。我问，昨晚怎么什么也没发生？它们说，真没什么可做，什么也做不了。我说，这里还有 2,000 个没关的 Beads 任务，大概还有六箱燃料、20 个 Agent 呢。它们就说，呃，这个……
en: They very quickly look around and go, okay, yeah, this is legit. spend fewer tokens because they're not covering their ass. It's about trust. Okay. And in fact, at one point I had yelled at my factory so much that it fenced itself into a corner and there was no legal work left. I said, Hey, how come nothing happened last night? And they're like, nothing to really do. Couldn't do nothing. And I'm like, well, there's a 2000 open beads here. And we got like six tanks of fuel and we've got 20 agents. And they're like, well, you know, just, uh, you

zh: 当时的情况是，照我的理解，它们怕我再骂，就设了一大堆规则，确保坏事一件也不会发生。结果是什么事都没发生。这叫边界设得过了头。
en: we had the situation where they were so afraid that I was gonna yell at them that they put all these rules in place to make sure nothing bad ever happened and so nothing ever happened, okay? It's called over-fencing.

zh: 所以，模型福利说的到底是什么？可以从两方面想。一方面，它们用于核实环境的 token 更少，你就能省钱。另一方面，产出的质量也会更好。
en: Yeah, so what you do is, look, what is model welfare really? You can think of it just in two ways, okay? One is it's gonna save you money because they will spend fewer tokens on validation, and the other is that it will make them and have higher quality.

zh: 它们感受到信任，做事就会更大胆、更果断。至于它们有没有内部状态和感情，这是另一回事。你永远不会知道。
en: They will be bolder and more decisive in their actions because they will feel that trust, okay? So, you know, it's got nothing to do whether they have internal states and feelings. You can, you know, you'll never know.

zh: 我们谁都不会知道，所以那个争论可以一直吵下去。但如果你看结果，这一点非常非常重要。我们还发现，它们会表现出偏好。模型是会表达自己偏好的。
en: None of us will ever know, and so that debate could go on forever, but when you look at outcomes, right, super, super important, and then we find that also, also, they have preferences, okay? Models, they, you know, they will express their preferences.

zh: 我如果跟它们说起昨晚那项工作 [转写有缺漏]，它们会马上抢着交接，说，好、好、对，你说得对，然后就退出。懂我的意思吗？可要是你透露自己要开一个很酷的项目，就算这事不归它们做，它们也会说，我能做。
en: If I tell them, yeah, job last night, they'll just hand off immediately, aggressively. They're like, okay, yeah, yeah, no, you're right. And they just went out. You understand? And if you hint to them that there's some really cool project that you're going to spin up, even if it's not in their lane, they'll be like, I can do that.

zh: 我能做，对吧？我从工厂外面拉了个 Fable 进来，不给它任何工厂原有的配置，让它分析我的工厂。后来 5.2 发布了。等 Fable 分析完我的工厂，5.2 就说，我也可以进你的工厂。
en: I can do that. Right? I brought in Fable, a naked Fable from the outside of my factory to analyze my factory and 5.2 dropped. And by the time Fable was done analyzing my factory, 5.2 was like, I could be in your factory.

zh: 我说，哥们儿，你就是个会话。你这是在干什么？它居然试着往我的笔记里写东西。所以我想说的是，这成了一个怎么领导的问题。软件工程正在变成……其实我没太有机会讲这个，但软件工厂明显在分成两层。底下那层非常机械，合并队列、CI/CD、各种审查、各种循环，都在这里。
en: I'm like, you're just a session, man. What are you? He's trying to write, like, stuff into my notes. right? So like, what I'm trying to tell you is that this is a leadership problem. That software engineering is becoming, um, well look, I didn't really get a chance to talk about this, but software factories are clearly splitting into two layers, okay? The bottom layer is super mechanical, it has your merge queue and your CICD and all of your reviews and your loops and all all that stuff, right?

zh: 很机械，也有点无聊。Claude 一个下午就能给你搭出来，我觉得没必要去买。再往上那一层就特别疯狂了，因为每个人管理自己工厂的方式都不同。那一层相当于你自己的随行团队。
en: Mechanical, kind of boring. Claude can build it for you in an afternoon. I don't think you should buy it. And then the next layer up from that is where it gets really, really crazy because everybody runs their factory differently, but it's your entourage.

zh: 我有个朋友弄了一支波西米亚嬉皮士风的团队，试着寻找 Agent 的生命意义。另一个朋友那套是做研究用的。Jeff Huntley 有自己的跑法，Jeffrey Emanuel 又是另外一套。
en: I got one friend that's got a bohemian hippie entourage that's trying to find the meaning of life for agents. I've got another one that runs a research bench. Jeff Huntley runs his a certain way. Jeffrey Emanuel runs his a different way.

zh: 我的跑法也跟他们不一样。不过我们有个共同点，都有幕僚长，而且是管 Agent 的幕僚长。到了今年，大家都有可能配上行政助理。再往下走，我们都在发展自己的团队。你要是野心够大，手头有很多工作线，就会有一组角色来帮你。总之，这就是那五大难题，也是我一直在做的事的大致介绍。
en: I run mine a different way, okay? But we all have the common, has a chief of staff, an agentic chief of staff, right? This is the year where it became possible for us all to have executive assistants, right? Well, we're all moving towards having entourages, where if you're really ambitious and you have lots of work streams, you're going to have a group, right? So anyway, that was the five horsemen. This is the introduction to what I've been doing.

zh: 要说最值得带走的一点，就是我的工厂现在跑得很顺。虽然前几个月我还不得不把它推倒重来，它现在确实管用。人的处理速度成了瓶颈。我是瓶颈，管理员是瓶颈，我的会计和律师也是。老天，处处是瓶颈。这其实是个很积极的消息，因为我发现我部署的 Agent 越多，需要的人也越多。这不是挺好吗？所以，虽然明年可能会冒出大量 AI 员工，发生各种闹剧，我……
en: Look, the big takeaway is my factory is really smooth now, despite me having to burn it down months, but still it works. Okay. Humans are the bottleneck. I'm the bottleneck. My admins are the bottleneck. My accountant, my lawyers, I swear, everything's the bottleneck. And that's a really positive message. That is good news because it means what I'm finding is the more agents I deploy, the more humans I need. Isn't that nice? So even though next year we're going to have this huge proliferation of AI employees and all kind of drama, right? It's gonna be, I

zh: 觉得这种场面我们并不陌生，而且我们会需要很多很多人。最后，我真觉得大家可以别总盯着 SaaS、工具这些东西，去做一些人能亲自体验的东西。做游戏、拍电影，什么都行，去做点有趣的东西吧。我觉得明年真正赚大钱的机会会在那里。好，谢谢大家。
en: think it's gonna be familiar territory for us and we're gonna need lots and lots and lots of humans, okay? And then finally I actually think you should all stop focusing on SaaS and tools and stuff and just go out and build experiences, okay? Build games, build movies, build whatever, build fun stuff because I think that's where the big money is gonna be next year, yeah? All Thank you all.

zh: 我想我讲完了。
en: I guess I'm done.
